findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh the displayed cache status
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback. The connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt is not invalidated, and this wrapper explicitly disables refetch-on-window-focus. When the wrapper is used without an onChanged callback (which its props permit), a successful deletion leaves the old timestamp and delete action visible until a full remount or reload. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful/settled cache deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Migration fabricates the last-updated time for every existing cache entry
findings.body: Adding this non-null column with DEFAULT NOW() stamps every pre-existing CalendarCache row with the migration time. The new UI presents this value as "Last updated", so immediately after deployment old cache data will be reported as having been refreshed at deployment even though its value may be nearly expired. Backfill from an existing source such as expiresAt minus the cache TTL where valid, or represent legacy timestamps as unknown until the cache is refreshed.

findings.title: Each cache warm rewrites all selected-calendar rows for the credential
findings.body: After populating cache data for the supplied selectedCalendars, this credential-wide update touches every SelectedCalendar row with that credential, including calendars and event types that were not part of the refresh. Because SelectedCalendar has an updatedAt field, this is a bulk physical update solely to change timestamps; the new cache-status endpoint reads CalendarCache.updatedAt instead, so this write does not affect the displayed status. Cache refreshes can be triggered repeatedly by webhook/cache workflows, causing avoidable row locks, WAL/MVCC churn, and contention for credentials with many event types. Remove this touch or limit it to the rows actually refreshed if another consumer truly needs it.

findings.title: The webhook helper cannot reliably update .env on GNU/Linux
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, the separate empty argument is treated as an input file, causing sed to exit with an error; because the script does not use `set -e`, it can still print that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated. This makes the added test helper unreliable on Linux. Use a portable temporary-file replacement or select the appropriate `sed -i` form per platform and fail when the replacement fails.
